segments.text: Legacy Decision Tree Chat asks customers to think like the menu.
Choose a category, follow a branch, repeat the context, and start over when the issue doesn't fit.
The friction gets worse when support and shopping live in different surfaces.
One interface explains, another acts, and the customer carries the journey between them.
For Bookly, the opportunity is bigger than replacing a legacy chatbot.
A unified concierge widget can connect, discovery, purchase, account services, fulfillment, recovery, and human help in one customer journey.
One identity and one conversation carry context across Bookly, while support, commerce, and fulfillment teams work from a shared order, inventory, policy, carrier, and case data.
This opportunity is already showing up in retail.
In live proof of concepts through peak season, 1-800-Flowers.com reached nearly 93% CSAT, double-digit points above its previous automation.
Hunter Douglas reports more than $1 million in revenue from conversations handled entirely by AI, with an average order value 85% higher among customers who engaged with the agent.
For Bookly, that is the value hypothesis, improve service, and help more customers complete their
purchases. Now, let's show how the future estate works. Today, we turned that value proposition
into a working real-time concierge with text, voice, live transcripts, semantic turn detection,
and natural interpretation. One conversation can open an exact book, select a format,
update the cart, begin checkout, investigate delivery problems, and resolve a return or
reach out to a person. Conversation is the control surface, but it is never the system
of record. That separation matters because fluent answers, fluent. Conversation is the control
surface, but it's never the system of record. That separation matters because a fluent answer
is not enough. Every price, order status, eligibility decision, and action must match
Bookly's actual data. The model handles dialogue and tool choice, while 29-type tools verify the
identity, rag retrieval, SQL database, transactions, and Visible Trace's own truth and consequence.
Bookly gets both sides of the experience, natural for the customer, deterministic,
and auditable for the business. For private or consequential actions, the system slows down on
purpose. Sign-in happens in a browser-owned form outside the model of conversation. Refund,
replacements, order changes, and shipping investigations follow one pattern. Prepare,
confirm, revalidate, and commit with a one-time token. A customer can move from discovery to
shopping, account help, delivery recovery, returns and refunds, and human escalation without
restarting or losing context the interface stays continuous while server controls preserve ownership
policy state in a durable audit trail what we just saw removes the burden from the customers
they can speak naturally discover the right book take action and see bookly respond without
leaving the conversation the impact is less effort faster resolution and more confidence
Contact stays intact, actions are visible, and consequential steps remain under control.
